GS.rationale: Goldman Sachs demonstrates strong fundamental health trajectory with Q1 026 EPS of $17.55 (second-highest in history), revenue of $17.23B (+14.4% YoY), and ROE of 19.8%. The firm is the #1 global M&A advisor with 32% market share and Advisory revenue surged 89% YoY, and record equities revenue of $5.3B was achieved. The strategic pivot away from consumer banking (which cost $7B+ in losses) back to core institutional strengths in Global Banking & Markets and Asset & Wealth Management is paying off. AUS reached a record $3.7T. However, valuation has expanded significantly: the stock trades at P/E 17.6x and P/B 2.36x, near the top of its 12-month range (P/E 12-18.4x, P/B 1.4-2.5x), suggesting the market is already pricing in much of the strong fundamental improvement. The business is highly cyclical (71% of revenue from Banking & Markets), and the FICC segment missed expectations in Q1. Cash flow generation is volatile quarter-to-quarter. The recent lifting of a 2018 Fed cease-and-desist order and an accelerated $5B buyback are positive near-term catalysts, but the stock's strong run (+80% over the past year) and current elevated multiples limit further upside. Macro backdrop is mixed: elevated VIX (19.3), rising oil ($99/bbl), and geopolitical tensions (Iran conflict) create headwinds for deal activity and trading, though the 10Y-2Y curve remains positive at 0.51%.
